facts.text: A load-haul-dump machine (LHD) is a low, long loader built for underground mines to scoop broken rock, carry it along narrow tunnels and dump it into a truck or chute.
facts.quote: A load-haul-dump machine (LHD) is a low, long loader built for underground mines, where it scoops broken rock, carries it along narrow tunnels and dumps it into a truck or a chute.

facts.text: A load-haul-dump machine (LHD) is also called a scoop or underground loader.
facts.quote: An LHD, also called a scoop or underground loader

facts.text: The operator of a load-haul-dump machine sits sideways in a low cab.
facts.quote: The operator sits sideways in a low cab

facts.text: New South Wales recorded 30 collisions involving load-haul-dump machines and personnel transports in underground coal mines in the 12 months to mid-2025.
facts.quote: New South Wales recorded 30 collisions involving LHDs and personnel transports in underground coal mines in the 12 months to mid-2025

facts.text: The load-haul-dump machines involved in the 30 collisions recorded in New South Wales underground coal mines in the 12 months to mid-2025 often carried bulky loads, such as concrete kibbles, that blocked the operator's view.
facts.quote: often with the LHD carrying bulky loads such as concrete kibbles that block the operator's view [Chapter 4]

facts.text: In New Zealand, an underground loader loading from a stockpile caught the body of a reversing truck with its bucket and tipped onto its side.
facts.quote: In New Zealand an underground loader loading from a stockpile caught the body of a reversing truck with its bucket and tipped onto its side [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Collision systems sold for underground machines slow and stop the machine.
facts.quote: Collision systems sold for underground machines slow and stop the machine

facts.text: Collision systems sold for underground machines depend on every person and machine carrying a tag.
facts.quote: Collision systems sold for underground machines slow and stop the machine but depend on every person and machine carrying a tag [Chapter 2].

facts.text: Safety evidence from underground operation does not automatically transfer to surface haul roads, or vice versa, because underground speeds and tunnel geometry differ from surface haul roads.
facts.quote: Underground speeds and tunnel geometry differ from surface haul roads, so evidence from one does not transfer automatically to the other [Chapter 4].

facts.text: A load-haul-dump machine's own bucket load can block the view ahead; the passage identifies the LHD as the clearest case of a machine whose own load creates a blind spot.
facts.quote: The LHD is also the clearest case of a machine whose own load creates the blind spot.
